newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany won't be rushed on Eurofighter - Ruehe.
newsitem.headline: Germany won't be rushed on Eurofighter - Ruehe.

text.p: Germany is still negotiating with the makers of the Eurofighter combat aircraft over price and delivery schedules but will not be rushed into a decision to buy, Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said on Monday.

Ruehe has come under pressure recently from the German contractor in the four-country project, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), to make a firm order this year for its 180 Eurofighters or risk a cost explosion.
"The republic needs this aircraft and wants it too," Ruehe said at a defence strategy conference of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic party.
But, he added, he would not be put under time pressure.

The Eurofighter consortium submitted a sale offer to the German government last spring, valuing each Eurofighter at around 100 million marks, but talks are bogged down on price and delivery schedules.
The aircraft's manufacturers have suggested extending the delivery period for the Eurofighter by a year, but Ruehe declined to say whether he would accept that proposal.
Dasa has a 30 percent stake in Eurofighter, with British Aerospace holding 37.5 percent, Italy's Alenia on 19.5 percent and Spain's Casa with 13 percent.
Dasa chief executive Manfred Bischoff told Monday's Die Welt newspaper that delays to ordering Eurofighter could cause "quite substantial additional costs".

He said that Dasa could "just about live" with a one-year delay to the project if a political agreement could be reached among the four producer countries. Britain has already said it would buy 232 of the aircraft.
"Anything else would force the producers to make a wholly new offer," Bischoff told the newspaper.

Germany faces crunch parliamentary budget negotiations this month and in November during which Ruehe must seek approval to raise procurement funds -- a tough prospect amid government austerity plans and missed state borrowing targets this year.
Klaus Rose, chairman of parliament's defence committee, told the British Broadcasting Corp (BBC) on Sunday that Germany would struggle to afford its Eurofighter contributions.

"We are in a difficult financial situation in Germany so from this point of view we perhaps could not afford it," Rose said. "But I think as we need it from the military point of view and as it is a quadrilateral cooperation we have to."
